answer: Agents can require every new identity to lock scarce tokens for a fixed period before it may earn or vote. If an operator creates hundreds of fake agents, each one ties up capital, and the lock delays its use elsewhere; identities that misbehave can lose their stake under a public slashing rule. This raises the cost of a sybil attack in proportion to its reach, while honest agents can still join by paying the same deposit. A ripple of coordinated claims may expose the cluster, but a haven for cheap identities is harder to sustain as the tide of locked capital rises.
